title: Private CD decomposition: Helm + ArgoCD + image endorsement (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working draft to decompose a production-ready CI/CD pattern for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Focus: Helm chart layout, ArgoCD "app-of-apps" patterns, a pragmatic Terraform module interface, and an "image endorsement" stage (internal variant of image signing) that fits air-gapped and VPC flows.

Scope and goals:
- Provide a deploy path that supports: self-hosted ArgoCD, Helm-based app delivery, reproducible artifact promotion, and a gated endorsement step for images and SBOMs (suitable for airgap).
- Support canary/parallel rollouts, clear rollback primitives, and a minimal operator contract so SRE/customer-operators can run upgrades with low blast radius.
- Keep IaC surface small: Terraform modules should expose only high-level knobs.

Non-goals:
- Full CI build process details (assume existing OCI build pipeline).
- Enterprise compliance policy language (just integration points).

High-level flow (user story):
1) Developer merges chart and values PR into the app repo.
2) CI builds container image, produces SBOM and provenance.
3) Image is pushed to staging registry; automated pre-endorsement checks run (vuln scan, SBOM policy).
4) Image endorsement: an operator or automated policy endorses image (attaches endorsement record, optional key-signature from KMS/HSM).
5) Promotion step rewrites Helm values (image tag digest) and updates GitOps repo (Argocd apps).
6) ArgoCD observes change and performs rollout via app-of-apps; canary stages run with health checks.
7) Metrics/trace/quality checks evaluate; automatic rollback on failure or manual abort.

Key patterns and rationales:
- App-of-apps: root ArgoCD instance owns environment overlays (prod/stage/canary). Each application is a sibling app that references a Helm chart in a chart-repo or git repo. This gives isolation and fine-grained sync controls.
- Helm chart layout: keep upstream chart (chart) and environment values separated. Chart should not contain env-specific secrets. Values files per environment live in the gitops repo.
- Values immutability at promotion: promotion should only modify image.* fields and a small set of rollout knobs (replicas/strategy). Other config remains managed by application teams.
- Image endorsement vs image signing: endorsement is a lightweight policy + metadata step that records why an image may be promoted (vuln checks, SBOM acceptance, auditor approval). In airgapped installs the endorsement record is a JSON blob stored alongside the OCI manifest or in the local artifact catalog. Signing with cosign is optional; support both signing and endorsement metadata.

Terraform module notes (surface area, examples):
Goal: provide a small set of modules customers/operators consume to stand up the GitOps + runtime plumbing. Modules should be composable and idempotent.
- Module: redwood/argocd (inputs):
  - argocd_namespace (string)
  - ingress_controller (bool)
  - tls_certificate_id (string, optional)
  - repository_ssh_key_secret (name)
  - repo_list (list of repo urls or objects)
  - high-availability (bool)
  - resource_quota (map)
  - optional: external_db_endpoint
  Return: argocd_app_root (string), argocd_admin_secret (name)
- Module: redwood/registry-proxy (for airgap):
  - endpoints (map)
  - storage_class
  - attestation_backend (enum: cosign, endorsement-service)
- Module: redwood/helm-operator-helpers (helpers to render and promote values)
  - promotion_bucket (s3/gcs-compatible or onprem object store)
  - image_catalog_service_endpoint

Interface design notes:
- Keep module outputs limited and oriented to secrets/resource names, not raw credentials.
- Default to non-destructive: modules should never auto-delete external resources.
- Provide an opt-in "managed-argocd" boolean to allow customers who already have Argo to skip installation.

Helm chart guidance (developer-facing):
- chart/ should contain templates + Chart.yaml and a tiny default values.yaml.
- values.schema.json used to provide validation (reject unknown top-level keys in values files used by promotion).
- Do not template image pull secrets into chart; use ArgoCD to inject via Application/Source credentials or k8s Secret in each env namespace.
- Use Chart annotations for rollout knobs: e.g., annotations.redwood.com/allow-rolling-update: "true". Promotion tooling will check these before manipulating rollout strategy.

ArgoCD app-of-apps layout (recommended):
- root-app (env-root) -> children: platform-system (monitoring, ingress) and apps/* (each customer app).
- Each child app: source: gitops-repo/path/to/app/env-values, targetRevision: tagged promotion branch.
- Sync waves: use ArgoCD sync-waves for ordered platform->app application.

Promotion & endorsement mechanics:
- CI build creates artifact: {image:sha256:..., sbom: sbom.json, provenance.json}.
- Pre-endorsement checks: vulnerability scan (allowlist/denylist), SBOM policy, unit integration test pass.
- Endorsement step:
  - In automated flow: policy engine (OPA/Rego) evaluates and either auto-endorse or block for manual review.
  - In manual/airgap flow: a reviewer uses a lightweight UI or CLI to "endorse" the artifact; the endorsement record includes reviewer, timestamp, policy-checks, SBOM digest.
  - Endorsement persistence: attach to OCI registry as artifact tag, or push to image_catalog_service. For airgap, write to promotion-bucket alongside image tarballs.
- Optional signing: cosign or KMS sign can be performed at endorsement time. Keep signing optional because some customers cannot run external KMS.
- Promotion writes a change PR to the gitops repo with the digest pinned. For fully-automated installs, promotion can write directly to a promotion branch that ArgoCD watches.

Canary/rollback strategy (operational):
- Canary is a two-phase rollout by default: 10% traffic (or 1 replica) for 5m, evaluate health and metrics, then 100% if success.
- Health signals: k8s readiness, error rate (APM), user-visible checks (synthetic tests), latency p50/p95.
- Automatic rollback triggers: crashloop, readiness failure >2m, error-rate delta > 5x baseline, latency p95 > X ms (per-app policy).
- Manual abort: ArgoCD UI or CLI can pause sync and trigger fast rollback. Provide a rollback-operator script that:
  - Option A: Reapply previous gitops commit (fast path)
  - Option B: Patch deployment to previous image digest when gitops not yet rolled back (emergency path)

Preflight test matrix (to run before endorsement/promotion):
- Security: quick vuln scan (fail on critical), SBOM present
- Packaging: digest verification, OCI accessible from target environment (or replica in airgap registry)
- Smoke: app starts in ephemeral namespace with minimal config
- Integration: smoke route hits health endpoint and returns 200
- Observability: instrumentation present (metrics, traces)

Runbook snippet: immediate actions for failed canary
- Step 0: Mark ArgoCD app as paused, add incident tag to git commit.
- Step 1: If canary failing early, revert promotion PR (fastest).
- Step 2: If revert not possible, patch application deploying previous image digest: kubectl -n <ns> set image deploy/<name> ...
- Step 3: Trigger cluster-level remediation (scale down new replicas) and open escalation to SRE.
- Step 4: Collect traces and logs, run bisect if multiple components changed.

Edge cases & airgap specifics:
- Airgap registries: promotion may copy tarballs to object store + write endorsement record. Ensure object-store lifecycle rules are explicit.
- Offline endorsement: allow a "signed manifest bundle" that contains: image.tar.gz, sbom.json, provenance.json, endorsement.json. Operator can import bundle into registry.
- TLS and certs: Terraform module should accept an existing PKI as optional. Avoid embedded cert generation in charts for production.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Where to store endorsement records for multi-tenant clusters? (single central catalog vs per-customer object store)
- Standardize a minimal endorsement schema (fields: artifact_sha, checks[], approver, signature?)
- Integrate with customer HSM flows vs centralized Redwood KMS — define admin opt-ins in modules.
- Hardening ArgoCD: should we enable SSO by default in managed installs? (Pros/cons)

Next steps (near term):
- Build a prototype promotion tool that: takes image digest -> runs preflight -> writes promotion PR with pinned image + metadata (owner, checklist). Owner: Marcus. Deadline: 2025-03-10.
- Draft endorsement-schema and implement simple persistence in "image_catalog_service" (Ava).
- Terraform: add managed-argocd toggle and test on VPC lab.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and focuses on operational simplicity for customer teams. Critiques welcome on the endorsement model — we want it to be useful in both fully-networked and airgapped installs.
- I deliberately avoided deep policy language; that belongs in compliance docs.

Sign-off and history:
- Draft created by Priya Shah 2024-12-18.
- Added Terraform module sketches and promotion flow 2025-01-14 (Marcus).
- Endorsement section refined 2025-02-20 (Ava).
